# Data engineering failures

<small>Source: [`R/errors-operations.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/r-dataexcept/blob/main/R/errors-operations.R) · Help: `?data_engineering_errors`</small>

Errors raised by batch data processing: a transformation step that failed,
an ETL job that did not complete, and a batch that could not be processed.
All inherit from `dataexcept_data_engineering_error`.

## Usage

```r
data_transformation_error(step, details = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

etl_job_error(job_name, message = NULL, parent = NULL, call = NULL)

batch_processing_error(batch_id, parent = NULL, call = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`step`
:   Name of the transformation step.

`details`
:   Optional detail, appended to the message.

`parent`
:   The condition that caused this one, or `NULL`.

`call`
:   The call to report, or `NULL`.

`job_name`
:   Name of the ETL job.

`message`
:   A message to use instead of the default.

`batch_id`
:   Identifier of the batch.

## Value

A condition inheriting from `dataexcept_data_engineering_error`.

## Examples

```r
process_batch <- function(id, rows) {
  tryCatch(
    sum(rows),
    error = function(e) stop(batch_processing_error(id, parent = e))
  )
}
err <- tryCatch(process_batch("2026-09-27", list("a", 1)), error = identity)
conditionMessage(err)

data_transformation_error("normalise_amounts", details = "12 rows had no currency")
```
